reasons: The cited clause (s.20(d)) is a flat mutual consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, so it fails the fallback (successor assignment on notice; consent not unreasonably withheld) and sits in the rule's walk-away zone for a Customer M&A event — 'deviation' is the correct classification.

The redline implements the preferred position directionally in our favour: unilateral Customer right to assign to affiliates/successors on notice, Vendor assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, residual mutual consent softened by a reasonableness standard, and an express no-termination/no-re-pricing statement on Customer change of control, per the redline guidance.
The conforming edit to s.3(c) ('except as permitted by Section 20(d)') is necessary because that covenant otherwise re-imposes the bar on Customer assignment; it is narrowly drawn.

The failed 'minimal edit p0142' check (ratio 0.815) is acceptable here: the original single sentence had to be restructured into asymmetric assignment rights, which cannot be achieved by insertion alone.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice, though it does not expressly mention the added change-of-control sentence; the rationale correctly notes Section 17 contains no Vendor change-of-control trigger, so that sentence is confirmatory rather than a duplicate flag — a minor drafting-scope point, not a defect.
